It's your machine, or at least it isn't the command Klippy sends. Klippy runs `explorer.exe /select, <path>` (`Klippy/Services/ExecutionPolicy.cs:901`), and every way of showing a path in Explorer goes through it. I ran that exact command here on your path, then asked Explorer what it had selected. The scratchpad window opened with `prolec-pirform-requests.md` selected. It also worked with the trailing `.` from your message on the end of the path.

So I can't reproduce it. If the selection really is missing for you, the likeliest cause is how Explorer is behaving on your machine at the moment, for example an existing Explorer window being reused. Restarting Explorer would rule that out. It could also be that the file was selected but the window opened without focus, which makes the highlight very faint; that one I haven't been able to check.

Yes, very likely. ExplorerTabUtility catches the window that `explorer.exe /select,` opens and turns it into a tab, and on two paths in its code (`ExplorerTabUtility/Hooks/ExplorerWatcher.cs`) the selection doesn't survive that:

- **The selection is copied too early.** When the new window registers, ETU hides it, reads what's selected (`GetSelectedItems(window)`), closes it, and opens a tab in your main window with that selection. It reads the selection straight away, before Explorer has necessarily applied `/select`, so it can copy an empty selection into the new tab.
- **A tab for that folder is already open.** With "reuse tabs" on, `OpenTabNavigateWithSelection` switches to the existing tab and returns before it selects anything, so the file is never selected.

It depends on timing: ETU was running during my test and the file was selected that time. That fits the first path, which works or fails depending on how quickly Explorer applies the selection. Turning ETU off would confirm it.

Klippy could avoid this by selecting the file through the shell API (`SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems`) instead of starting `explorer.exe /select,`. That API selects in an existing window when the folder is already open, so ETU would never get a new window to convert. I haven't tested that against ETU.

I've opened PR #48, which fixes this so the file ends up selected with ExplorerTabUtility running: https://github.com/seankearon/klippy/pull/48

My earlier suggestion was wrong. Calling `SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems` instead of starting Explorer doesn't fix it. With ETU running it returns an error (E_FAIL) even when the folder is already open, and without ETU it opens a new window rather than selecting in an existing tab that isn't the active one. My earlier 5/5 result was partly ETU putting back the selection a window had when it closed.

The PR does it differently. Klippy still starts `explorer.exe /select,` as before. Then, for 4 seconds, it selects the file once in each Explorer window or tab showing that folder, which catches the tab ETU moves the window into. This runs on a background thread, so it doesn't delay the toast. It's written as hand-coded COM calls in the new `Klippy/Services/ExplorerSelection.cs`, because the Windows build is NativeAOT and the usual late-bound COM isn't available there.

Results on your machine, with a new folder for each trial:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| ETU running, folder not open | 0/8 | 5/5 |
| ETU running, folder already open in a tab | 0/5 | 6/6 |
| ETU stopped | selected | selected |

- The same code compiled with NativeAOT, in a small standalone harness, selected the file 4/4 times with ETU running.
- The NativeAOT publish of `Klippy.Desktop` succeeds with no new warnings.
- All 1000 tests pass.
- I haven't tried it in the full running app, because that is driven by the hotkey UI.

I stopped and restarted ETU three times during testing. It's running again, but the Explorer windows you had open earlier (Downloads, the Pirform screenshots folder and others) aren't any more. I don't know whether you closed them or the ETU restarts did.
